ORDER With the consent of both the parties matter is heard finally.

2. This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellant/Insurance Company under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short "MV Act") for setting aside the impugned award dated 30.6.2010 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Datia in Claim Case No.131/2009 whereby learned Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.7,27,500/- with interest of 8% per annum from the date of filing the claim petition.

3. Brief facts of the case are that on 14.5.2009 when the deceased Matadeen Sahu was coming towards Datia from village Unnav with his wife respondent No.1/Pukkhan Devi as a pillion rider and when they reached near village Parasari Unnav-Datia Road, then respondent No.6 by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:343 2 MA-1808-2010 driving his motorcycle being Registration No.UP93P2201 in a rash and negligent manner, dashed the motorcycle being driven by deceased Matadeen.
Deceased Matadeen and his wife fell down.
Both of them sustained grievous injuries and during treatment, deceased Matadeen died.
Respondents No.2 to 5 are the sons of the deceased and at the time of incident, the offending vehicle was insured by the appellant/Insurance Company.

Respondents no.1 to 5/claimants preferred a Claim Petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act before the Reliance Gen.Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt.Pukhan Devi on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79263039/

sentences.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Datia for compensation of Rs.70,66,000/-, wherein it was alleged that at the time of incident, deceased was a healthy person aged about 44 years and was earning income of Rs.24,000/- per month from the shop of ready-made garments.
The Claims Tribunal after scrutinizing the evidence available on record, awarded the compensation of Rs.7,27,500/- in favour of respondents No.1 to 5.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award, appellant has preferred this miscellaneous appeal.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that impugned award is bad in law, against the law and facts and evidence available on record.
Learned Tribunal has grossly erred in not considering the testimony of witness claimant Pukkhan Devi (PW-1) and eyewitness Brijkishore Soni (PW-2).
Brijkishore Soni (PW-2), has categorically admitted in his cross-examination that a report has been lodged by respondent No.6 against deceased Matadeen also.

It is further submitted that accident was caused by deceased Matadeen himself by driving his motorcycle rashly and negligently and as there was a contributory negligence of the deceased, therefore, the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:343 3 MA-1808-2010 appellant/Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation in the matter.
The impugned award is against the settled principles of claims jurisprudence.
Hence, he prays that the impugned award be set aside.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant in support of his contention placed reliance upon the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the cases of Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay vs. Laxman Iyer & Anr. reported in (2003) 8 SCC 731, Bijoy Kumar Dugar vs. Bidya Dhar Dutta & Ors. reported in (2006) 3 SCC 242, Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation & Anr. vs. K. Hemalatha &
Ors. reported in 2008 ACJ 2170, New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Mangal & Ors. reported in 2008 ACJ 2174 and this Court in the case of United India Insurance Company vs. Brijkishore Jatav & Anr.

6.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondents no.1 to 5/claimants opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection by submitting that the impugned award passed by the Tribunal below is just and proper and does not deserve for any interference.
7. Counsel for both the parties are heard at length and perused the record of Tribunal below with due care.

8. Pukkhan Devi (PW-1), who was sitting as a pillion rider on the motorcycle driven by her husband deceased Matadeen, categorically admits in para 10 of her cross-examination that at the time of accident, both the motorcycles dashed to each other.

9. Brijkishore Soni (PW-2), who was eyewitness of the incident also admits in his deposition that the motorcycle driven by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:343 4 MA-1808-2010 deceased Matadeen directly hit the motorcycle driven by respondent No.6, but Pukkhan Devi (PW-1) and Brijkishore Soni (PW-2) both of them categorically denied in their cross-examination that the accident was caused due to contributory negligence of the deceased.

Pukkhan Devi (PW-1)
stated in her deposition that respondent No.6 was driving his motorcycle rashly and negligently and he hit the motorcycle driven by her husband.

Brijkishore Soni (PW-2) also denied that the accident Reliance Gen.Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt.Pukhan Devi on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79263039/
2

sentences.text: was caused due to negligence of deceased, therefore, both these witnesses have not supported the case of the appellant regarding contributory negligence of the deceased.

10. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that an FIR has also been lodged against deceased Matadeen about the aforesaid accident but the appellant did not examine any witness before the Tribunal below.
No such copy of FIR was proved before the Tribunal below.
Pukkhan Devi (PW- 1) did not admit in her cross-examination that any FIR has been lodged against her husband Matadeen.
Therefore, in absence of material evidence, the appellant has failed to prove that any FIR has been lodged against deceased Matadeen in respect of the aforesaid accident.
Therefore, in absence of the evidence adduced by the appellant, the Tribunal below has rightly held that the present case is not a case of contributory negligence.
All the citations relied upon by learned counsel for the appellant are not applicable in the instant case.

11. Apart from above, on the basis of the statements of claimant Pukkhan Devi (PW-1), eyewitness Brijkishore Soni (PW-2), FIR NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:343 5 MA-1808-2010 (Ex/P/2), charge sheet (Annexure P/1), spot map (Annexure P/3), merg intimation (Annexure P/4),
it is proved that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.6 Kamlesh Pal and at the time of incident, the motorcycle of respondent No.6 Kamlesh Pal was insured with the appellant/Insurance Company.
12. Now the moot question to be addressed as to whether the Tribunal below is justified in awarding the compensation of Rs.7,27,500/- to the respondents No.1 to 5 or not?

13. From perusal of paras 13 to 20 of the impugned award, it appears that Tribunal below has considered all the medical expenses and has awarded compensation under the head of special diet,
transportation, attendant, pain and suffering, loss of income and other expenses.
The Tribunal below has rightly considered the age of the deceased i.e. 44 years and his annual income of Rs.54,000/- from the business of ready-made garments.

14. Considering the evidence available on record, facts and circumstances of the case and arguments advanced by learned counsel for both the parties, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Tribunal below has rightly considered the income of deceased and looking to age of the deceased,
multiplier of 15 was rightly applied by the Tribunal below.
Therefore, the compensation awarded by Tribunal below is adequate, just and proper and does not deserve any interference.

In the result, this appeal fails and is hereby dismissed and the award dated 30.6.2010 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Datia is hereby affirmed.

Both the parties shall bear their own expenses.
